newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia, C&W talk on cutting phone monopoly.
newsitem.headline: Latvia, C&W talk on cutting phone monopoly.

text.p: Latvia has launched talks to shorten the monopoly period of national phone operator Lattelekom, in which Britain's Cable & Wireless has a big stake, Prime Minister Andris Shkele said on Friday.
He said both sides could reach agreement on the controversial issue after around six months.
"The monopoly situation has to be changed and we have embarked on talks already," Shkele told a news conference, saying he met C&W officials on April 24.
"I expect the basic discussions to be over within the coming half year and both sides to be satisfied," Shkele said.
Lattelekom is 49 percent-owned by Tilts Communications, formed by C&W, Telecom Finland and the World Bank's International Finance Corp.
The group was given monopoly status until 2013 but pressure by politicians who say that Lattekelom is too expensive has forced talks to shorten the monopoly period to 2003.
Lattelekom has said it would not be able to continue the costly upgrading of Latvia's outdated telephone system if its monopoly period was cut short.
Since 1994, Tilts has invested $160.3 million in Latvia and it reported a 1996 after-tax profit of 4.08 million lats against 3.29 million lats the year before.
It said this profit was not enough to keep up the pace of modernisation, which was a third completed.
